questions.problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ with vertices $(-1,0),(2,0),(2,2),$ and $(-1,2),$ traversed counterclockwise. Using the flux form of Green's theorem, express the flux of the vector field
$F(x,y)={x}^{2}y\,i+5xy\,j$
through $C$ as a repeated integral.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14157147/assets/265d27ad87a7f114bd2a32a5f48cbfedb13192abf48f9b759c4ed635e71ff144.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)=5xy.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2xy,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =5x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+5x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(2y+5)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the rectangle $C$ with vertices $(0,0),(3,0),(3,2),$ and $(0,2),$  traversed counterclockwise. Using the flux form of Green's theorem, express the flux of the vector field
$F(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,i+12xy\,j$
through $C$ as a repeated integral.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14157147/assets/23066b23aebf332921c22a0439a414ade8dffd2a270641d186da0ed0e9488821.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=12xy.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2x{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =12x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 2\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x{y}^{2}+12x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}2x({y}^{2}+6)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨x+\sqrt{y},\,y+\sqrt{x}⟩
$$

through the boundary of the region enclosed by the curve $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and the line $y=0$ for $-\frac{\pi }{2}\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14157147/assets/e570374b37c116e32c3a7762b8cf09a28bdbb3e06b5e67e25837902a89bcd264.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=x+\sqrt{y}$ and $Q(x,y)=y+\sqrt{x}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-\frac{\pi }{2}\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{cos}⁡x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}y\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,dx \\  & =2{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =2(1-(-1)) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
